About me

Gianna posted on February 22nd, 2024 in Uncategorized

Introducing myself again after one year!

Hi! My name is Gianna, your chronically sleep-deprived girlie! Being a sheltered little girl all my life (strict parents life), college in Southville really opened up many doors for me-- actually being allowed to go out of the house, having friends for the first time, going out with friends, and even having free quality tertiary education!

I dread being asked about hobbies and interests as they mostly revolve around singing and studying (anthropology, Ph culture and diversity, linguistics, psychology). But!! Now, I am getting to experience life outside academics and being the perfect daughter, so I know I'll discover many things that I like soon!

One thing I am sure about myself is that I want to make a change in the lives of my fellow Filipinos, so now that I am allowed to go out, I spend my time in community development. I love meeting different people as they enrich my life with meaning and purpose!

Throughout my life, I have received many opportunities to rise above my station. It is my life's mission to help as many Filipinos in the same way.

Activity 1: STAR Performer

Gianna posted on February 23rd, 2024 in Activities

Hey everyone,

As a person who wishes to make a difference, one of my role models is Maria Ylagan Orosa, most known as the woman behind the banana ketchup.

She studied about food technology abroad at the University of Seattle in Washington, but refused the offer to work there. Instead, she returned to the Philippines and enriched everyone's lives with her experience. Her inventions revolutionized local food and food preservation and fought against malnutrition during and after the war, saving countless lives.

Activity 2: Self-Esteem Questionnaire

Gianna posted on February 27th, 2024 in Activities

Here are my reflections!

1. What do you consider as your strengths based on this tool?

My strengths lie in optimism and self-efficacy.

I normally think that the world wants me around and I can achieve my dreams.

 

2. How are these helpful in your life as an adolescent/student?

As a college student, the belief in myself and that I can surpass difficulty can help

keep my head high during exam weeks and major projects.

This keeps my motivation and outputs consistent.

 

3. What do you consider as your developmental areas?

My developmental area is people-pleasing and relaxing. I think most of my problems

arise from my fear of being alone and unloved once again.

Furthermore, as my friends would say, I should relax and not feel bad about treating myself.

 

4. How are these related to your scores in the Big 5 personality profile?

My two highest scores are on agreeableness, explaining my people-pleasing tendencies, and

conscientiousness, explaining my drive to succeed.

Activity 3: Jackson's Vocational Interest Survey

Gianna posted on February 27th, 2024 in Activities

Here are my reflections!

1. What were your initial reactions with your JVIS results? Were there any surprises or patterns you noticed?

Quoting Dea when she saw my results, I would say it is “very me.” Except for the fact that HRM is one of my highest. I never can see myself working in a usual office setting and managing people.

For the most part, according to JVIS, I am definitely a proud humanista. I love spending time, studying, and making a difference in the lives of people and society. Most of my decisions in life have been guided by this principle which includes taking up psychology and joining different youth organizations.

Lagi’t lagi, para sa bayan ♡!

 

2. How do your JVIS test results resonate with your current personal achievements and successes?

My work styles imply that I am a goal-oriented workaholic, academic validation girlboss who has the willpower to keep working on her (mostly academic and professional) goals, come what may.

This has been the reason for my academic success–willpower. I am not a pabebe girl, pero walang makakapigil sakin (huh????) in the achievement of my super high goals. I aim high and I prepare and work hard in order to achieve that.

Notes after rereading: What was I thinking???? Hahahahahaha!

 

3. Considering both your JVIS results and personal achievements, are there any areas where you feel you could further leverage your strengths or explore new opportunities?

Not really, as I am already trying to be more involved with the community through my youth organizations. These develop my leadership, time management, and people skills, and grant me connections to the government, business owners, and like-minded pag-asa ng bayans, all of which helps me become the best person that I can be.

Activity 4: Locus of Control

Gianna posted on April 16th, 2024 in Activities

Here are my reflections!

1. What are the implications of your LOC score for the kind of achiever that you want to be?

My locus of control score implies that I have both external and internal locus of control, which is objectively true. There are some situations wherein I work super hard, but endup failing on it due to factors outside my control. When this happens, I want to have peace of mind and not blame myself for these factors. This is the achiever that I want to be–the ‘such is life’ achiever. Sometimes, life is not fair. Sometimes, failure happens, and that is okay. This is not my fault, and that is unconditional positive self-regard.

 

2. Does your LOC score ring true to you, given the tendencies listed above? Why or why not?

Yes. One thing I noticed while answering the questions is that sometimes, I would attribute my failures to myself, but not my success. That is an unhelpful and unhealthy behavior that lowers my self-esteem.

 

3. How did your LOC affect your ability to succeed in academics (and non-academic activities) and the demands it made of you? What kind of LOC score would have been suitable now that you are in your 2nd year of college? Why?

My internal locus of control led me to controlling every part of my life to comply with requirements during my college years. I now schedule my day, my months, and my year, just to keep my head above the figurative flood of deadlines, my fear of failures and the unknown. As a second year in college, an appropriate score would still be the half. As responsibilities and the intensity of studies increase, we students need to believe in our capability to change things, as well as the fact that there are extraneous variables that we cannot control. Failures may happen. If so, we can be discouraged, but we must keep pushing through. Such is life!

Activity 6: Productivity

Gianna posted on April 30th, 2024 in Activities

Here are my reflections!

1. What do you want to achieve in terms of productivity?

I am a very productive person, especially during the fifth weeks of every term. However, what I need is more time! 5 hours of sleep a night and then 10 hours of school a day leaves me less than 10 hours to do work (while taking periodic naps when I get lightheaded), which is not enough when I am learning a new concept, memorizing terms, creating notes, searching for practice tests. Sometimes, I wish I were a robot and not worry about sleep or other physiological needs anymore, haha.

With that said:

  • I should sleep more than 5 hours a day and take more breaks.

  • When lightheaded, try to eat or stand up and walk around or talk to someone inside the house.

  • Set timers when doing tasks, so I can work more quickly and spend more time doing other tasks.

    •  

    2. Set deadlines for implementing your strategies and achieving your goals.

    I have only 5 days before the exam week, so these strategies must be implemented as early as 7 pm today, after arriving home!

     

    3. How will you hold yourself accountable for following through your action plan?

    As a natural-born anxiety-ridden and overly self-critical individual, this is not anything new to me. I always keep myself accountable in every little thing I do! One effective way of keeping me from submitting late is telling myself that one wrong step will result in me not finishing my college education! How very positive ⋆｡°✩.

    /sarcasm

     

    Processing Questions #1

    Gianna posted on May 23rd, 2024 in Activities

    Here are my reflections!

    1. How did it feel to share your setback with a partner? Was it difficult to be open about it?

    The initial thought of sharing this setback with a partner is that he might think, “Hay nako, Gianna, lagi nalang acads ang nasa isip.” Now that I think about it, why pretend, when every word is true?

     

    2. What was the most challenging part about admitting the truths about your setback?

    I have always been an independent person – laughing and crying alone. The most challenging part of admitting it is the notion that I need help. Externally, I look like I have my entire life on track, but do I actually?

     

    3. How did changing your attitude towards the setback influence your perspective on it?

    Initially, I thought of this as a setback that this extracurricular may ruin my grades because it is taking so much studying time away from me. However, I changed my mindset to “If I can pull this off, I can definitely survive my third year.” It gave me the willpower to meticulously plan my months in advance – when I should start on major submissions, when I should pass them, when I should study, etc.

     

    Processing Questions #2

    Gianna posted on May 30th, 2024 in Activities

    Here are my reflections!

    1. How did the process of analyzing the setback help you understand what went wrong and how to avoid similar issues in the future?

    Nothing really went wrong as it is merely a conflict in schedule. I think what was wrong is me approaching this challenge with an anxious mental state. I should have known better and trusted myself more.

     

    2. Can you discuss a specific solution or alternative you proposed to address the setback? Why did you choose this approach?

    The specific solution is for me to up my time management game! Before, I used to study the entire week before exam week (Week 5), but Mamma Mia’s filming is in Week 5, from Thursday to Saturday. Initially, Fridays to Sundays of Week 5 are the days where I do not get up from my study desk, studying every single lesson. Now that these days are not free anymore as I am playing as Sophie, I had to study earlier, frequently, and in lesser amounts. I didn’t have time for elaborate studying before Week 5 since we usually went home at 9 pm and I needed to sleep early to recover from my sickness (that I somehow had since Week 3 and never gotten better ever since.)

     

    3. How did creating an action plan help in turning the setback into an opportunity?

    Creating an action plan made me feel like I still had control over my life despite all the time I didn’t have anymore. It made me less anxious since I focused on what I can do, instead of lamenting all that I cannot. Now, during exam week, I did study less, but I trusted myself more, not stressing myself too much, leading to a hopefully better academic performance than before!
